evidence.summary: Protocol server axum router registers 5 endpoints: GET /healthz, GET /info, POST /rpc, GET /ws, GET /rpcws
POST /rpc handler maps a JSON-RPC response to 200 OK and a notification to 202 Accepted
GET /ws WebSocket handler: pushes kernel events, discards inbound RPC responses (one-way by design)
GET /rpcws WebSocket handler: full-duplex JSON-RPC plus event push via tokio::select!
stdio server loop: one JSON-RPC request per input line, one response per output line
JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope types RpcRequest / RpcResponse / RpcError and the standard error codes
Kernel::dispatch is the single RPC method router shared by stdio, HTTP and WebSocket (22 methods)
Kernel::handle_rpc parses the envelope, enforces jsonrpc=="2.0", suppresses notifications and maps error strings to JSON-RPC codes
Event enum defines the WebSocket push payload variants (tag = "kind", snake_case)

unknowns: crates/ide-kernel, crates/ide-kernel-core and crates/editcore were NOT read (out of scope for this agent). Handler behaviour descriptions for /api/doc/*, the editcore mirror routes and the Tauri doc_*/editcore commands are derived from the calling code in the shell crates only, not from the kernel implementations.

The protocol server (crates/ide-shell-protocol) registers NO auth on its axum routes (POST /rpc, GET /info, GET /healthz, GET /ws, GET /rpcws). It binds the configured --addr (default 127.0.0.1:8123) but does not validate Host/Origin or require a token.
The web server (crates/ide-shell-web) and the protocol server both default to port 8123 - they cannot run simultaneously without changing --addr / IDE_SHELL_WEB_ADDR.
GET /ws is one-way by design: inbound JSON-RPC requests are dispatched but the response is deliberately discarded (crates/ide-shell-protocol/src/bin/ide-shell-protocol-server.rs:190).

crates/ide-shell-protocol's register_provider RPC method always fails with 'register_provider is in-process only' (crates/ide-shell-protocol/src/lib.rs:1133) - providers can only be bound at process startup.

The web server's OPTIONS catch-all (crates/ide-shell-web/src/lib.rs:1381) is unreachable in practice: auth.check returns 204 'preflight-no-cors' for OPTIONS before routing (crates/ide-shell-web/src/auth.rs:137).

The TUI's :open/:e command opens files through ide_kernel::Document (crates/ide-shell/src/app.rs:164) rather than through the desktop/web path_safety sandbox; no 4 MB / project-root sandbox is applied beyond the size check.

crates/ide-shell-protocol's own Kernel (crates/ide-shell-protocol/src/lib.rs:407) is a separate, headless implementation from ide-shell's App and from ide_kernel::Document - the two are not wired to each other in the code read here.
No test files (*/tests/*.rs) were treated as runtime surface; they were only used to confirm behaviour.
